"MONSTERVERSE BOX – REALISTIC 3D KAIJU SANDBOX

Create a highly realistic, fully playable 3D kaiju sandbox game inspired by the MonsterVerse universe.

The game should feel like a combination of a realistic physics sandbox, an open-world destruction simulator, and a cinematic giant monster battle game.

IMPORTANT: Do not create just a prototype menu or a static environment. Build actual playable gameplay systems with functional controls, physics, interactions, AI, and destruction.

1. GAMEPLAY AND MAIN FEATURES

The game must include:

- Open-world free roam.
- Playable giant monsters.
- AI-controlled monsters.
- Monster-versus-monster battles.
- Destructible buildings and environments.
- Realistic ragdoll physics.
- Environmental destruction.
- Dynamic weather and time of day.
- Realistic monster animations.
- Combat abilities and special attacks.
- Sandbox spawning system.
- Custom battle setup.

Players should be able to freely explore the environment, control monsters, spawn characters, destroy buildings, and watch AI monsters fight.

2. MAIN MENU

Create a polished cinematic main menu.

Menu options:

- PLAY
- FREE ROAM
- BATTLE ARENA
- SANDBOX
- MONSTER COLLECTION
- SETTINGS

Use a realistic 3D background featuring a giant monster standing in a destroyed city.

Add atmospheric lighting, fog, moving clouds, cinematic camera movement, and subtle environmental animations.

The interface should look professional, clean, modern, and easy to navigate.

3. MONSTER ROSTER

Include a monster selection system featuring:

- Godzilla 2014
- Godzilla 2019
- Godzilla 2021
- Godzilla Evolved
- King Kong 2017
- King Kong 2021
- King Kong 2024
- Mechagodzilla
- King Ghidorah
- Rodan
- Mothra
- Shimo
- Scylla
- Tiamat

Each monster should have its own:

- 3D model.
- Accurate proportions.
- Unique animations.
- Walking and running.
- Idle animations.
- Attacks.
- Special abilities.
- Health and stamina.
- Combat statistics.
- Sound effects.

Do not make every monster use the same animations or attacks.

4. REALISTIC COMBAT SYSTEM

Implement a fully functional combat system.

Combat moves should include:

- Light attacks.
- Heavy attacks.
- Punches.
- Kicks.
- Tail attacks.
- Bites.
- Grabs.
- Throws.
- Roars.
- Blocking.
- Dodging.
- Special abilities.

Godzilla should have atomic breath, tail attacks, stomps, bites, and atomic-powered attacks.

Kong should have punches, kicks, grabs, throws, axe attacks, and powerful ground slams.

Every attack should have appropriate animations, sound effects, hit detection, and impact reactions.

5. REALISTIC RAGDOLL AND PHYSICS

This is one of the most important features.

Create a sophisticated physics-based reaction system.

When monsters are hit:

- Their bodies should react naturally.
- They should lose balance.
- They should stumble.
- They should fall when hit with enough force.
- They should be pushed backward depending on attack strength.
- They should collide with buildings and environmental objects.

When monsters fall:

- Their bodies should interact with the ground.
- They should experience realistic landing impacts.
- They should slide across surfaces depending on momentum and friction.
- Their limbs should react naturally.
- Their bodies should gradually recover and stand up.

Add realistic collision detection, mass, weight, gravity, friction, momentum, and impact forces.

Do not make ragdolls look stiff or robotic.

6. DESTRUCTIBLE CITY

Create a large, realistic Hong Kong-inspired city.

The environment should contain:

- Tall skyscrapers.
- Apartment buildings.
- Commercial buildings.
- Roads.
- Bridges.
- Streetlights.
- Vehicles.
- Parking areas.
- Sidewalks.
- Street decorations.
- Rooftop structures.

Buildings must be destructible.

Destruction features:

- Buildings develop cracks and structural damage.
- Windows shatter.
- Walls break apart.
- Building sections collapse.
- Debris falls onto roads.
- Dust clouds appear during destruction.
- Vehicles can be crushed.
- Street objec

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D kaiju sandbox inspired by MonsterVerse, with a cinematic menu, open-world combat, monsters, destructible structures, weather, and sandbox controls.

## Requirements
- Include free roam, battle arena, sandbox, monster collection, and settings modes.
- Provide a roster of 14 titans with distinct silhouettes, statistics, and abilities.
- Include combat, AI battles, movement, environmental destruction, vehicles, debris, weather, and time-of-day controls.
- Use a polished realistic 3D visual style and responsive desktop/mobile controls.
- Build actual gameplay rather than a static prototype menu.

## Decisions
- Implemented as a browser game using Three.js loaded via CDN.
- Used procedurally modeled stylized-realistic titans and an extensive generated city rather than external 3D assets.
- Used single-file gameplay logic in `game.js` with shared skeleton-like anatomy and monster-specific variants.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created the cinematic HTML interface and professional menu styling.
- Added the Three.js city, harbor, roads, skyline, streetlights, vehicles, rain, clouds, lighting, fog, and camera behavior.
- Implemented 14 titan roster entries and dynamically constructed titan models.
- Implemented player movement, sprinting, combat actions, monster AI, health, stamina/energy, battle setup, spawning, building damage, debris, and dust.
- Added sandbox weather/time controls and a titan collection panel.
- Added keyboard, touch, mouse-drag, and scroll controls.
- Added desktop and mobile responsive UI.
- Added initial syntax-fix candidate for a time-slider line.

### Active
- The game implementation is complete enough to serve, but the final syntax and browser validation is pending because `node --check game.js` found an unmatched parenthesis in the time-slider handler.

### Blocked
- `game.js` currently has a syntax error at line 100:
  `Unexpected token ')'`
- Browser capture and visual validation could not be completed until the syntax error is resolved.

## Next Move
1. Fix the unmatched parenthesis in `$('#time-slider').oninput` in `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js:100`.
2. Run `node --check game.js`.
3. Start the project using `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/start.sh`.
4. Open `http://localhost:3002` with `playwright-cli`.
5. Capture and inspect a latest JPEG, then validate menu navigation and gameplay entry.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: Main menu, HUD, panels, and modal structure.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/style.css`: Full responsive visual system and interface styling.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js`: Three.js scene, city, titan models, combat, AI, physics reactions, weather, and controls.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/start.sh`: Project start command.

## Important Context
- `game.js` is uncommitted and also includes the only known blocking issue at the time-slider line.
- The implementation uses CDN-hosted Three.js at `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.161.0/build/three.module.js`.
- The project expects to be available on port `3002`.
- The user has not asked for, and the agent did not claim, GPU hardware acceleration or successful browser verification.
